chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: Johnny's girl band, lost photographs and few women musicians
summary: Johnny's ten-or-twelve piece girl band gave concerts; his wife's belongings were auctioned; there were few professional women musicians in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did your brother's girl band have a special name? Was it his name on it--or was it...

No, I had a...got pictures around here somewhere but I don't know where all that stuff is...of his band, you know, the girl and everything, and see, when his wife died here about four or five years ago, she packed all that stuff in Bekins Van & Storage Company, and
it was all sold for auction, you know, and I don't know what was all in there 'cause she never had any relatives or anything, and she give all her money to Braille Institute, and so, uh...
You don't know what happened to all those pictures and things. How big a band was the girl band that he had?
He had about ten or twelve in his band, and he'd direct them, you know, and...

Oh, no, I don't think they got that good but they used to play for, you know, their own little concerts and things, which, after the band broke up, there was two or three of them that continued... They got into the band...er, dance field then, you know. Yeah.
And you don't remember the names of any of those professionals?
No. I know Anna and her sister but I can't think of their last name.
Were there very many women working professionally as musicians here in Los Angeles?
